key_insight: Visually grounding objects by their roles, intentions, and relations (scenario comprehension) is a fundamentally harder and complementary task to standard referring-expression grounding; the paper introduces RSC to expose and quantify this gap.
problem_solved: Existing benchmarks let models succeed by matching named categories; this work targets the challenge of identifying targets that must be inferred from roles, intentions and relational context rather than explicit naming.
method: Introduce Referring Scenario Comprehension (RSC), a benchmark of images paired with queries that require role- and relation-based inference rather than literal reference.
Annotate scenario-style queries emphasizing roles, intentions and relations, and define an evaluation protocol that contrasts RSC performance with standard referring-expression tasks.
Evaluate existing visual grounding models on RSC, analyze common failure modes, and highlight the need for better relational and pragmatic reasoning.
impact: RSC reveals a gap in current vision–language models and provides a focused benchmark to drive progress on relational, role-aware, and pragmatic grounding — essential for real-world scene understanding and human-like multimodal reasoning.
visual_elements: Example image with an overlaid scenario query (e.g., “the person about to hand over an item”) and the correct target bounding box highlighted.
Bar chart comparing model accuracy on standard referring-expression benchmarks vs RSC to show the performance drop.
Pipeline diagram illustrating scenario comprehension: input image + role/intention query → relational reasoning module → grounded output.
Failure-case montage showing common errors (category-match shortcuts, wrong-role selection, relation confusion) with short captions.
paper_title: Beyond Referring Expressions: Scenario Comprehension Visual Grounding
paper_authors: Ruozhen He, Nisarg A. Shah, Qihua Dong, Zilin Xiao, Jaywon Koo
